title: Secure Vendor Disbursements: How to Utilize Payouts API Verification in Manufacturing
summary: Are hidden payment risks threatening your supply chain? Learn how a secure payouts API verification process stops procurement fraud and protects your business.
body_markdown:
Managing high-value payouts across a complex network of suppliers, raw material vendors, and logistics partners leaves little room for error. When processing dozens or hundreds of high-value invoices weekly, finance operations face a constant security challenge. A single compromised invoice or modified bank routing detail can quietly divert hundreds of thousands of dollars before anyone notices the discrepancy.


As supply chains scale globally, traditional payment workflows struggle to keep pace with modern threat vectors. Relying on manual checks, paper forms, or fragmented banking portals creates operational bottlenecks and exposes cash flow to sophisticated financial schemes. Protecting business capital requires shifting from reactive fraud detection to automated, pre-payment verification embedded directly into your financial infrastructure.


## The Growing Threat of Procurement Fraud in Manufacturing


Procurement and payout processes remain primary targets for bad actors due to the sheer volume and size of B2B transactions. According to the[FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center 2025 Internet Crime Report](https://www.ic3.gov/AnnualReport/Reports/2025_IC3Report.pdf) , Business Email Compromise (BEC) and payment fraud schemes accounted for over $3 billion in exposed losses in a single year. These attacks frequently exploit the gap between invoice approval and final funds disbursement.


In industrial and supply chain environments, single incidents carry severe financial weight. Research referenced in the[J.P. Morgan Payments Fraud Education Guide](https://www.jpmorgan.com/insights/payments/security-trust/payments-fraud-education-guide) highlights that a vast majority of organizations experience payments fraud annually, with B2B supply chains suffering average losses exceeding $135,000 per incident. Beyond the immediate capital loss, fraudulent diversions disrupt production schedules, strain supplier relationships, and create significant administrative burdens during recovery efforts.


## What are Some Examples of Fraud in Procurement?


Understanding how bad actors infiltrate payout workflows is the first step toward building stronger controls. In vendor disbursement workflows, procurement fraud typically occurs when unauthorized entities manipulate supplier details or invoice data prior to settlement. Common tactics include:


- **Vendor Impersonation and Bank Detail Manipulation:** Perpetrators intercept communication channels or compromise business email accounts to pose as existing suppliers. They then submit updated banking information, directing future disbursements to fraudulent accounts.
- **Fake Invoice Schemes:** Bad actors generate illegitimate invoices for goods or services that were never ordered or delivered, relying on lax verification controls to push payments through standard approval cycles.
- **Internal Overpayment and Kickback Schemes:** Malicious internal actors collaborate with external entities to approve inflated invoices, alter payment destinations, or duplicate disbursements for personal gain.


Relying on manual verification, such as calling vendors to confirm account changes or manually cross-referencing bank routing numbers, creates significant operational friction. It slows down processing times, introduces human error, and fails to scale as transaction volume grows.

This automated approach delivers several key operational advantages:


- **Pre-Payment Account Validation:** Confirms that the target bank account is active and registered to the intended business entity before initiating the transfer.

- **Seamless Multi-Rail Routing:** Allows disbursements to be routed across preferred local and international payment channels without compromising verification standards.
